supporting: flexbox and grid as flexible layout tools

claims.claim: Responsive web design is an approach for layouts that work well across screen sizes and resolutions, not a separate technology.
Plain HTML text normally reflows as the viewport changes, while a fixed-width page can cause scrolling or excess empty space.
Flexible grids and modern layout methods such as Flexbox and Grid support responsive layouts without targeting every device size.
The viewport meta value width=device-width tells mobile browsers to use the device width for the viewport.
Media constrained by max-width: 100% can avoid overflowing its container; supplying one oversized image to small screens can waste bandwidth.
Responsive design must retain usable text, structure, labels, and alternatives; W3C guidance recommends clear structure, descriptive links, and text alternatives.
